rationale:
Evidence: all 60 development trials in every iteration ended off_track, with no completions. Progress has never exceeded about 0.17, and max_error sits at 0.060 to 0.067, just past the 0.06 m limit. Body width cannot widen that limit, so the limiting factor is steering and sensing.

What the history shows: the sensor row moved forward (y 0.04, then 0.06, then 0.08) with sensor_size 0.016, wheel_track 0.14 and kp 3.0 was the only change that moved the score materially (about 40 to 58). Iterations 7 and 8 scored identically (58.1734) despite changes to kd, wheel_track and base_speed. Iteration 9 widened the span to plus or minus 0.06 m and scored worse (55.13), so the plus or minus 0.03 m span is the better layout. Iteration 10 (sensor_size 0.012, kd 1.5, kp 3.0) is the best design so far at 58.8527, with the best oval and slalom progress.

Change, relative to iteration 10: (1) kp 3.0 to 3.5. Oscillation is about 0.17 and the robot drifts past 0.06 m at the sharper bends, so I add a little steering authority. kd stays at 1.5 to damp the extra gain. (2) Everything else is held fixed, including sensor layout, sensor_size 0.012, base_speed 1.5, wheel_track 0.14, mass 0.6, ki 0.0 and line_loss 'last_direction'. This keeps the change attributable to one controller variable.

Expected result: a small gain over 58.85, with progress above about 0.18 and max_error slightly lower. Completion is still unlikely. The main risk is that kp 3.5 adds overshoot, which would show as higher steering_oscillation and an earlier off-track exit. If that happens, the fallback is the iteration 10 design.
